$description: #271 harvest lane B — ONLY the non-unanimous rules. One row per rule. Columns = each consulted system's position, VERBATIM or `silent`. `silent` = the system speaks on the component but not on this rule. `unreachable` = the fetch failed (see SOURCES.refused) — that is NOT silence. Options are for Dave; the recommendation is THE LANE'S, not his and not canon.
$rule: Unanimous rules are NOT here. Where the KIND agrees and the NUMBER differs, that is non-unanimous (the #270 radio→dropdown finding) and it is here.

rows.rule: At what list length does a record-list get pagination?

positions.Polaris: Paginate when the current list contains more than 50 items.
positions.IBM Carbon: When there is too much data to display on one page
positions.Ant Design: When it will take a long time to load/render all items.
positions.USWDS: silent — the page carries no when-to-use section at all
positions.NN/g: silent on a number; argues against infinite scroll instead

options: Adopt Polaris's 50 as our number.
Carry no number: gate on "more than one screen of rows" (device-relative, testable in a fixture).
Carry no number and no gate — pagination stays a composer's judgement, prose only.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. 50 is one system's number with no research cited, and a 40-row table on a phone already needs pagination. This is the exact shape of s270-D1 — if Dave rules a number here he should rule it the same way (provisional, with a tripwire).

rows.rule: May a Tag be interactive (a link or button)?

positions.GOV.UK: Do not use tags to create links, buttons or other interactive elements
positions.IBM Carbon: Do not use tags as links that direct you to an entirely different page
positions.USWDS: Users frequently confuse tags as buttons.
positions.Ant Design: silent — ships closable and checkable tags without comment
positions.ours: our meta SHIPS a Tag link variant and only forbids making static tags LOOK interactive

options: Retire the Tag link variant; tags become static labels only.
Keep it but fence it: a Tag link may only filter IN PLACE, never navigate (this is exactly what Carbon's wording leaves open).
Keep it as is and record the three-system disagreement on the meta.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. Carbon's objection is specifically to NAVIGATION, not to interaction; a removable filter chip is a tag that acts and every system ships one. Option 2 satisfies all three objections without losing a variant we already built.

rows.rule: Is a Tag a KEYWORD or a STATUS?

positions.IBM Carbon: Use tags to label, categorize, or organize items using keywords that describe
positions.Ant Design: It can be used to tag by dimension or property.
positions.GOV.UK: Use the Tag component to show users the status of something.
positions.Polaris: Use a single word to describe the tone of an object.
positions.Adobe Spectrum: Badges are used for showing a small amount of color-categorized metadata
positions.USWDS: one `tag` component does keyword, count AND new-content jobs
positions.ours: tags = keyword ("content composition"), status-indicator = state. Two components.

options: Confirm our split (keyword vs state) and note that GOV.UK/Polaris quotes about "tags" must be read onto our Status-indicator, never onto our Tags.
Merge: one chip component with a semantic variant, as USWDS does.
Confirm the split AND rename one of them so no external prose can be mis-filed.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Our split is the sharper of the two designs and Carbon + Ant back the keyword reading. But this must be WRITTEN DOWN, because four systems use the words differently and any future harvest will mis-file quotes without it.

rows.rule: How many slices may a pie or donut carry?

positions.Datawrapper: If you have more than five shares, consider a stacked column
positions.roles.json (ours): chart-pie when: "composition, no centre figure, ≤ 5 parts"
positions.our metas: antiPatterns[0] on BOTH pie and donut: "More than 6 slices (dv-pie-009 — combine into 'Other')"
positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: silent on a number; "difficult to accurately compare the size of the segments"
positions.NN/g: silent on a number; against the family entirely

options: 5 everywhere: change dv-pie-009 to 5 and keep roles.json.
6 everywhere: change roles.json's pie `when` to ≤ 6.
Keep both on purpose: 5 is the SELECTION cut (above it, choose something else), 6 is the RENDER ceiling (above it, the component refuses). Write that distinction down.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3, then a one-line note on both metas. Datawrapper's 5 is a choice threshold and dv-pie-009's 6 is a drawing limit — they are not actually the same rule, but nothing in the repo says so, so today it reads as a defect.

rows.rule: Is a donut better or worse than a pie?

positions.roles.json (ours): donut is the composition DEFAULT (weight 80); pie is 48
positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: the centre can be a good way of making space to include more information
positions.NN/g: made even less effective by the whitespace in the middle

options: Keep the ordering: our centre-total discriminator is a REASON, and FT gives the same reason.
Flip it: pie becomes the default and donut is the exception when a centre total earns its place.
Keep the ordering and add NN/g's caution to both metas as a documented dissent.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. NN/g's objection is to using either for comparison, which our `when` already excludes (composition only, parts sum to a whole). The FT independently reaches our exact discriminator, which is the strongest single corroboration in this slice.

rows.rule: What separates a progress reading from an allowance reading inside the one Meter?

positions.Adobe Spectrum: Their progress is determined by user actions, rather than system actions.
positions.IBM Carbon: Use a determinate progress bar when the progress can be calculated
positions.ours (s210-D1): "keep as one meter" — progress is a SEMANTIC VARIANT; no discriminator is written between the variants

options: Adopt Spectrum's test verbatim as the variant discriminator: user-driven ⇒ meter/allowance, system-driven ⇒ progress.
Keep the allowance test we already have (full = BLOCKED, not done) and write it onto the variant explicitly.
Both: full=blocked is the allowance test, user-vs-system is the progress/allowance test, and they must agree.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. s210-D1 is ruled and this is not a re-open. But the variants currently have NO written discriminator, so a composer cannot pick one — and "full means blocked" is our own, domain-true, and testable. Spectrum's test is worth quoting as EXTERNAL support, not adopting as the rule.

rows.rule: May more than one accordion section be open at once?

positions.NN/g: make sure to give people the capability to open multiple sections at a time
positions.Ant Design: an Accordion is by definition the Collapse variant that allows only one panel expanded
positions.GOV.UK: silent on the rule; ships a Show-all-sections control, which implies multi
positions.USWDS: silent on the rule; ships both bordered and multiselectable variants
positions.ours: silent — our meta says nothing about it

options: Multi-open is the default (NN/g, and GOV.UK's show-all control implies it).
Single-open is the default; multi is a variant.
Both are variants and the composer picks; the meta names the trade-off.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. GOV.UK's Show-all-sections button only makes sense in a multi-open accordion, and we already inherit GOV.UK-shaped accordion behaviour. Ant is naming a different component with the same word.

rows.rule: Does Carousel stay in the library?

positions.NN/g: some people will only see the first frame or none at all
positions.NN/g (title): Consider Using a Hero Image Instead of a Carousel
positions.Ant Design: When there is a group of content on the same level.
positions.GOV.UK / USWDS / IBM Carbon / Polaris: NO CAROUSEL COMPONENT EXISTS — four systems' worth of structural silence
positions.ours: PROPOSED #210 wave-4 lane C; not registered, not ruled; autoplay OFF proposed

options: Drop it. Four reference systems ship none and NN/g says don't.
Keep it, unratified, with a `when` written as a warning and a hard autoplay-off default.
Keep and ratify it as a normal component with a positive `when`.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. It is already unratified, so nothing is lost by leaving it there with an honest negative `when` — and a fintech marketing surface will ask for one whatever we write. Option 3 is the one the evidence does not support.

rows.rule: Is there a maximum number of cards in a card collection?

positions.USWDS: Consider limiting the number of items in each collection to six or fewer.

options: Adopt 6 as a soft ceiling above which cards yield to list-items or table.
No number; yield to table on the COMPARISON test instead ("if a field is read down a column, it is a table").
Both: 6 as a warning, the comparison test as the gate.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. USWDS's 6 applies to their `collection` component, not their `card` — importing it onto our Cards would be a quote lifted out of its component. The comparison test is the one that actually discriminates.

rows.rule: What separates a table from a list of records — field count, or purpose?

positions.roles.json (ours): list-items: "≤ 3 fields per item, tappable" · table: "default, read-mostly"
positions.Polaris: A resource list isn’t a data table
If your use case is more about finding and taking action on objects
A data table is a form of data visualization.
positions.IBM Carbon: Avoid using a list for complex data
positions.GOV.UK: Do not use it for tabular data or a simple list of information or tasks (summary-list, via #270)
positions.USWDS: When you need to display tabular information, such as statistical data.

options: Keep the field count (already adopted s252-D1); Polaris's purpose test becomes prose on the meta.
Replace the field count with the purpose test: analysis ⇒ table, action ⇒ list.
Both, ANDed: a list is ≤ 3 fields AND action-oriented; anything else is a table.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. The two tests agree on almost every real case and disagree only on the 5-field row of orders that are all links — which is exactly the fintech case we will hit. ANDing them sends that row to the table, which is the right answer.

rows.rule: When is a bar chart horizontal rather than vertical?

positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: Good when the data are not time series and labels have long category names
positions.Datawrapper: If you have more than approximately 10 categories
positions.ours: NO RULE — orientation is a variant with no criterion, and our AP1 only forbids negatives on the horizontal form

options: Adopt the FT test: long category labels or non-time-series ⇒ horizontal.
Adopt the Datawrapper count: > ~10 categories ⇒ horizontal.
Both, ORed — either condition makes it horizontal.
No rule; orientation stays a composer's choice.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. Both tests are about the same failure — labels that will not fit under a column — and they catch different halves of it. This is the largest completely-absent rule found in the chart family.

rows.rule: How many series may a grouped bar chart carry?

positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: Can become tricky to read with more than 2 series
positions.ours (chart-line): series 1–5 on one continuous time axis

options: Adopt 2 as a soft ceiling for grouped bars, above which use stacked or small multiples.
Adopt chart-line's 1–5 for consistency across the family.
No ceiling.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2, with the FT's 2 recorded as a caution. A hard 2 would make a four-quarter grouped comparison illegal, which is a normal fintech chart; but the family should not have a 5-series line and an unbounded bar.

rows.rule: When does composition-over-time stop being a stacked area and become stacked columns?

positions.Datawrapper: If you have less than ten or so dates, consider a stacked column
Area charts work best if you have many dates.
positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: seeing change in components can be very difficult
positions.ours: no date count on either side

options: Adopt ~10 dates as the cut: fewer ⇒ stacked bar, more ⇒ stacked area.
No number; use "the reader must read individual values" ⇒ stacked bar.
No rule.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is a single-source number, so it should be ruled the way s270-D1 was — provisional, with a tripwire — but it fills a genuine hole: today a 4-quarter split can legally be drawn as a stacked area, which is the worst option for it.

rows.rule: Which intent word gates chart-combo?

positions.FT Visual Vocabulary: showing the relationship between an amount (columns) and a rate (line)
positions.FT (filing): listed under CORRELATION first, and again under Change v Time
positions.roles.json (ours): "two measures in different units over one axis", answers = change-over-time only
positions.IBM Carbon: the intent buckets exist (Comparisons · Trends · Part-to-whole · Correlations · Connections · Geospatial) but per-chart prose was unreachable
positions.Datawrapper: has a dual-axis guide but it carries no selection criterion

options: Keep change-over-time only.
Add relationship: answers becomes [change-over-time, relationship], as chart-stacked-area already carries two.
Keep one word and record the FT's second filing as a known gap.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. chart-stacked-area already proves the two-word pattern is legal on our answers axis, and today a composer whose claim is "revenue against margin rate" is gated to Chart-scatter, which cannot draw it.

rows.rule: Which intent word gates the butterfly pair?

positions.FT (filing): population pyramid is filed under DISTRIBUTION
positions.roles.json (ours): "exactly two series mirrored, categories ≥ 6", answers = comparison
positions.everyone else: silent — no other system ships a butterfly

options: Keep comparison only.
Add distribution: answers becomes [comparison, distribution].
Keep comparison and note that a population-pyramid claim must reach it through comparison.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. Our butterfly's canonical uses are inflow-vs-outflow and actual-vs-target, which are comparisons; the pyramid case is real but rare in fintech, and widening the gate costs more than it buys. Recorded so the decision is visible, not silent.

rows.rule: Must a Stat card carry a delta?

positions.ours (meta when): shape = one-measure × value-and-delta AND series = none AND delta != none
positions.roles.json (ours): "default — label · value · delta · period, no series"
positions.Ant Design: When want to highlight some data.
When want to display statistic data with description.
positions.IBM Carbon: Use tiles to group related information in flexible containers.

options: Yes, delta required. A bare number is not a Stat card and needs a named home.
No: delta becomes optional and the gate drops to "one measure, no series".
Yes, required — and account-card becomes the named home for a bare balance.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. It keeps the role's fences intact (no series ⇒ not a KPI tile; no delta ⇒ not a Stat card) and it gives the bare-number case a real destination instead of leaving it homeless. Ant's Statistic shows the alternative design and it is looser than ours by a long way.

rows.rule: What IS Summary — a count board or a review receipt?
rows.kind: internal (found by this lane, not a system disagreement)

positions.roles.json (ours): "n × count as a key/value list, 6–12 cols" — a status-surface count board
positions.our meta (ours): "A key/value list for confirming details before or after an action (a payment review, a receipt)"
positions.GOV.UK: Do not use it for tabular data or a simple list of information or tasks (summary-list)
positions.Ant Design: Commonly displayed on the details page. (Descriptions)

options: One component, two variants (counts and receipt), one `when` covering both.
Two components: the count board stays in status-surface, the receipt moves out of the role.
Keep one and rewrite roles.json's `when` to match the meta (receipt), losing the count board.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. The shape is identical (name left, value right, optional total) and only the reading differs; splitting would duplicate a spec. But the mismatch must be closed — right now the role and the meta describe different components.

rows.rule: What are the copy rules for a status chip, and may ABSENCE of a chip mean a state?

positions.Polaris: Use a single word to describe the tone of an object.
Always describe the tone in the past tense.
positions.GOV.UK: Sometimes a single status is enough.
positions.Adobe Spectrum: When status lights have a semantic meaning, they should use semantic variant colors.
positions.ours: NO COPY RULE for the label at all

options: Adopt both Polaris rules (single word, past tense) as copy guidance.
Adopt them AND GOV.UK's absence-as-state pattern (no chip = the default state).
Adopt the copy rules only; forbid absence-as-state as a colour-alone-style failure.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. Past-tense single words fit our RAG set exactly (approved · cancelled · declined · pending — three of four are already past tense). Absence-as-state is a real GOV.UK pattern but it hides the state from a screen reader, which is the same failure our AP0 already forbids.

rows.rule: How many colour-coded categories may a legend carry?

positions.Adobe Spectrum: The ideal usage for these is when there are 8 or fewer categories
positions.NN/g: color should not be used to communicate information about quantitative
positions.ours: no ceiling on legend; the isoluminant categorical set's size is a token question

options: Adopt 8 as the legend's ceiling.
Rule that the ceiling belongs to the PALETTE (the isoluminant set), not the legend, and point the legend at it.
No ceiling.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 2. A legend with 12 entries is not wrong if 12 series are distinguishable; the real constraint is how many isoluminant categorical colours we have. Putting the number on the legend would hide it from the place that determines it.

rows.rule: Should a table ever yield to a chart?

positions.USWDS: consider a bar graph, infographic, or other type of chart
positions.Polaris: A data table is a form of data visualization.
positions.ours: NO RULE crosses record-list into chart-panel, in either direction

options: Add a record-list → chart-panel antiPattern on table: complex relationships belong in a chart.
Leave it. Role boundaries are FFF-function boundaries and a cross-role `when` would blur the axis.
Add it as prose on the meta, not as a gate clause.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. It is a real and useful designer rule, but making it a gate clause would need "complex relationship" to be machine-checkable, and it is not. Prose keeps it visible without breaking s251-D3's three-axis independence.

rows.rule: How tightly is Tree fenced?

positions.IBM Carbon: When you only need one level of nested information.
As the primary navigation in a product’s UI.
positions.Ant Design: Almost anything can be represented in a tree structure.
positions.roles.json (ours): "records nest" — no depth floor, no navigation exclusion

options: Import both Carbon exclusions as antiPatterns (single level ⇒ list-items; never primary nav ⇒ sidebar-nav).
Import the single-level exclusion only.
Keep roles.json as is; the exclusions are prose.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Both exclusions point at components we already have (list-items, sidebar-nav), which is exactly the shape our other antiPatterns take, and "records nest" alone would let a two-item flat list become a tree.

rows.rule: Is there a LOWER bound on pie slices?

positions.Datawrapper: Pie charts might be unnecessary if you only want to show two values
positions.ours: no floor — a 2-slice pie is currently legal

options: Adopt >= 3 parts as the floor; a two-part split is a sentence or an amount-display, not a chart.
No floor.
Floor of 3 for pie, and route the 2-part case to meter (one value against its complement).
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 3. The two-part composition case is real in fintech (used vs remaining allowance) and we already have the right component for it — that IS a limits-meter reading. Routing it there rather than banning it gives the composer somewhere to go.

rows.rule: What does a SUPERSEDED component's `when` say?

positions.ours (filter-toolbar-bar AP1): Consuming View-options instead of Segmented-control for the view switch — View-options was superseded 2026-07-24
positions.ours (view-options meta): reads as a live recommendation: "A view control that lets users select different presentation formats"

options: Give it a `when` that says "never — use Segmented-control".
Remove it from the library.
Leave it and rely on filter-toolbar-bar's antiPattern to catch misuse.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. Option 3 is the status quo and it failed once already — the supersession is recorded on a DIFFERENT component's antiPattern, where nobody choosing a view switch would look.

rows.rule: Are alias metas exempt from a when-completeness gate?
rows.note: progress-bar.meta.json is the same kind of thin alias and is equally affected by this decision, but progress-bar is slice A's component; it is recorded here as a note so `component` stays a single existing stem.
rows.kind: internal (mechanism, bites before the whens land)

positions.ours (s210-D5): progress-bar.meta.json and limits-meter.meta.json are thin category aliases of meter.meta.json; writing spec into them is an antiPattern
positions.ours (this harvest): any gate requiring a `when` on every meta would FORCE that breach

options: Exempt aliases explicitly: the gate reads the parent's `when`.
Allow a `when` on an alias only if it is a verbatim pointer to the parent.
Do not build a when-completeness gate at all.
rows.recommendation: THE LANE RECOMMENDS option 1. It is the only option that keeps s210-D5 intact. Flagged here because it must be decided BEFORE any `when` lands as a gated field, not after.
